To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the stochastic QSSAs performed for GRNs with different absolute values of mRNA and/or protein half-lives can measure the intrinsic noise at protein level accurately.

the stochastic QSSAs can be used as a good choice to quantify the intrinsic noise at protein level for large gene regulatory networks, provided the absolute values of half lives of mRNA and protein involved in the network is known.

the accuracy level of the stochastic QSSAs performed for GRNs critically depends on the absolute values (and not abundance level) of mRNA and protein half lives involved in the corresponding networks.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a stochastic Q-SSA model that can be used to predict the intrinsic noise in GRN with reasonable accuracy.
the question whether QSSA models can be used to quantify intrinsic noise accurately.
the question whether QSSA is a suitable model for quantifying intrinsic noise accurately.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the QSSA model is a good choice for intrinsic noise quantifications for GRNs, provided the absolute values of mRNA and/or protein half-lives are known.
for the GRNs considered in this study, the stochastic QSA is a good alternative to the mechanistic models for quantifying intrinsic noise, especially for the protein species.
QSSA can be used for quantifying intrinsic noise for any GRN, if we have the half-life values for mRNA and/or protein involved.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

for GRNs with low bursting frequency, the stochastic QssA model can be considered for intrinsic noise quantifications, but for those with high bursting frequency, the mechanistic model is the only choice.
QSSA is not always a good choice for intrinsic noise quantifications and it should be used with care.
the accuracy of a stochastic QSA model in quantifying intrinsic noise is dependent on the absolute values and not on the abundance levels of the mRNA and/or protein species involved in the GRN.
The main takeaway from our work is that
QSSA can be a good alternative to SSA performed for detailed mechanistic model for intrinsic noise quantifications for GRNs exhibiting switching behaviors.
QSSA models are suitable for intrinsic noise quantifications only for the combinations of absolute values for mRNA and protein half-life values that are capable of generating a large burst frequency.
the QSSA models can be used to predict the intrinsic noise in GRNs with greater accuracy, if the half-lives of mRNA and protein are chosen judiciously.
